text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Marie Curie, born Maria Sklodowska, was born in Warsaw on November 7, 1867, the daughter of a secondary-school teacher. [D]

In 1920 Curie learned that she had a double cataract; her vision became so impaired that she wrote lecture notes in huge letters, and only after four operations, between 1923 and 1930, could she again do exacting laboratory work and drive a car. [D]
In a November 1920 letter to her sister Bronya, Curie wrote that radium perhaps had something to do with her troubles, but that this could not be affirmed with certainty. [D]
Her cataracts are regarded as an early documented example of radiation cataract. [R]
Curie's fingers were severely burned from handling radioactive materials with her bare hands while preparing radium standards. [D]

During the First World War Curie directed the Red Cross Radiology Service, set up France's first military radiology centers, and equipped 20 mobile X-ray vehicles, the first ready by late October 1914. [D]

In 1925 Curie took part in a French Academy of Medicine commission that recommended lead screens and periodic blood tests for workers handling radioactive materials, and she required Radium Institute staff to have regular blood counts. [D]

In May 1934 Curie went home sick from her laboratory and never returned; specialists who suspected tuberculosis advised a sanatorium stay, and a medical expert from Geneva diagnosed an incurable blood disorder. [D]

Curie's mother, Bronislawa Sklodowska, died in May 1878 of tuberculosis at age 42, after a five-year illness, when Marie was ten; her eldest sister, Zosia, died of typhus caught from a boarder when Marie was eight. [D]

With Pierre Curie, whom she married in 1895, she discovered polonium and radium; she shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics, received the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, and directed the Curie Laboratory of the Radium Institute. Pierre Curie died in 1906. [D]

list.item: Occupational exposure to ionizing radiation over decades of radium research and X-ray work: active, confirmed [S]
Chronic radiodermatitis of the fingertips, with thin, scarred skin: active, confirmed [S]

Initial anemia workup in primary care: CBC with differential and reticulocyte count, blood film, vitamin B12, folate, ferritin, LDH, bilirubin, and kidney function. Guideline: Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of adult aplastic anaemia: A British Society for Haematology Guideline (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia and cataract monographs (2026) [S]

Supportive care: irradiated, leukocyte-depleted red cells for symptomatic anemia; platelet thresholds set by hematology; same-day assessment for a temperature of 38 °C or higher; avoid aspirin and NSAIDs. Guideline: Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of adult aplastic anaemia: A British Society for Haematology Guideline (2024) [S]

Record cumulative occupational radiation exposure, stop further exposure while counts recover, and review shielding and dosimetry for laboratory staff with occupational health. Guideline: Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of adult aplastic anaemia: A British Society for Haematology Guideline (2024) [S]

First-line immunosuppressive therapy given by hematology: horse antithymocyte globulin with cyclosporine and eltrombopag, plus acyclovir prophylaxis; inactivated vaccines only. Guideline: Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of adult aplastic anaemia: A British Society for Haematology Guideline (2024) [S]

Monitor CBC weekly during the first months of treatment, with kidney function, potassium, and ALT every two weeks on cyclosporine and eltrombopag. Guideline: Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of adult aplastic anaemia: A British Society for Haematology Guideline (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia and cataract monographs (2026) [S]

Comprehensive dilated eye examination with best-corrected acuity, intraocular pressure, slit-lamp examination, and a functional vision assessment; YAG laser capsulotomy when capsule opacification limits daily tasks; eye examinations every one to two years afterward. Guideline: Cataract in the Adult Eye Preferred Practice Pattern (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia and cataract monographs (2026) [S]
